explanation: Maintaining direct eye contact in Russia — during a handshake, in conversation, and especially when clinking glasses for a toast — is read as a sign of sincerity, and looking away can come across as evasive. This applies in both everyday social situations and business settings.
local_tip: Make steady eye contact during greetings and toasts; it's expected there and signals honesty rather than confrontation.

also_check.note: Prolonged direct eye contact can feel intimidating, especially with superiors; brief glances are more common.
Direct eye contact is expected in business as a sign of confidence and honesty.
Eye contact between unrelated men and women is typically kept brief out of modesty.

sources.title: Non-verbal confusion #2: Once more unto the breach
